article_title: Enabling Blind and Visually Impaired Individuals to Pursue Careers in Science
citation: L. Petitdemange and S. Nashed. (2025). ENABLING BLIND AND VISUALLY IMPAIRED INDIVIDUALS TO PURSUE CAREERS IN SCIENCE. SF2A 2025. https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.17620
title: Set of tactile and auditory teaching artifacts for astronomy developed with and for BVI audiences
description: A suite of hands-on educational materials designed by BVI scientists for inclusive astronomy outreach. It includes a magnetic-plate Milky Way model where sprinkled iron filings provide "a granular tactile representation that vividly conveys the density of stars in specific regions"; a cord-and-bead model of planetary distances; thermoformed tactile diagrams annotated in Braille; a real-time observational device producing tactile relief prints; and an eclipse demonstration converting captured light intensity into sound so the phenomenon is perceived "not through vision, but through sound".
requirements: precise verbal guidance and detailed descriptions accompanying all activities
design involvement of BVI scientists to ensure full accessibility
target_learners: BVI outreach participants of all levels and degrees of visual impairment
target_learning_goals: comprehension of abstract astronomical concepts such as apparent solar motion, lunar phases, seasons, eclipses and galactic structure
examples: The eclipse device: an opaque sphere orbits a luminous sphere while a camera converts light intensity to sound, so the sound's intensity decreases during the transit
